stories.headline: Anthropic's amended S-1 says future models may 'imminently' meet its AI-accelerated R&D threshold

key_facts.fact: In its amended S-1 (S-1/A) filed with the SEC on Nov 2, 2026, Anthropic added a risk factor saying internal estimates and expectations for future models indicate it 'may imminently meet' its Responsible Scaling Policy's definition of 'dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI'.
key_facts.excerpt: our internal estimates and our expectations regarding future models, rather than our current models, indicate that we may imminently meet our Responsible Scaling Policy's definition of "dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI."

key_facts.fact: Anthropic says it has not designated any current model as exceeding the threshold and continues to assess the underlying data.
key_facts.excerpt: We have not designated any of our current models as exceeding this threshold, and we continue to assess the underlying data.

key_facts.fact: The filing admits Anthropic has in the past failed to spot a significant acceleration in its rate of development until after it occurred, because its evidence comes largely from lagging indicators.
key_facts.excerpt: "we have in the past not identified, and may in the future not identify, a significant acceleration in our rate of development until after it has occurred."

key_facts.fact: Anthropic says it does not anticipate being able to safely use Claude to fully autonomously design and build successive frontier models without meaningful human supervision, and is considering RSP updates to keep humans in control of frontier model development.
key_facts.excerpt: we are considering updates to our Responsible Scaling Policy to keep humans in control of frontier model development at Anthropic.

key_facts.fact: Under RSP version 3.4 (effective July 8, 2026), the 'dramatic acceleration' route is defined as observing or expecting double the rate of progress in aggregate AI capabilities, measured over at least three model generations and attributable to automated research.
key_facts.excerpt: defined as observing or expecting "double the rate of progress" in aggregate AI capabilities ... measured over at least three model generations

key_facts.fact: Compared with the October S-1, the amendment changes the tense on missed accelerations and adds that Anthropic is weighing requiring human review of certain research decisions.
key_facts.excerpt: It is considering RSP updates to keep humans in control of frontier model development, and to require human review of certain research decisions.

stories.headline: Anthropic S-1/A: Q3 revenue ~$17B, $895B compute commitments; IPO investors push ~$1.5T valuation

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's amended S-1 shows Q3 2026 revenue of roughly $17 billion, up about 1,127% year over year, but sequential growth slowed to ~47% from 144% in Q2.
key_facts.excerpt: During its third quarter, Anthropic generated roughly $17 billion in revenue, up about 1,127% from the same period last year... Third-quarter revenue increased around 47%, a steep drop from 144% growth in Q2

key_facts.fact: Q3 net loss was $23.3 billion (vs $12.1B a year earlier), including a $21.9B non-cash fair-value loss on convertible notes; operating expenses rose 292% to $17.5B and Anthropic swung to a $567M operating loss from a $974M Q2 operating profit.
key_facts.excerpt: The latest third quarter figure includes a $21.9 billion loss related to an adjustment in the fair value of convertible notes... It flipped from an operating profit of $974 million in the second quarter... back to a negative $567 million

key_facts.fact: Anthropic disclosed purchase commitments and lease agreements of about $895.4 billion, substantially all for compute and infrastructure; about $70B falls due in the year through September 2027 and ~$448B before end-2030.
key_facts.excerpt: Substantially all of Anthropic's $895 billion of commitments are related to computing-power costs and infrastructure... Roughly $448 billion of that is expected to be incurred before the end of 2030, though about $70 billion of the commitments are due in the year through September 2027.

key_facts.fact: The Q3 operating loss was driven mainly by $5B of short-term compute bought at higher prices and $2B of non-cash charges for a donation-matching program; price cuts (including Opus 5.5) and discounts cut Q3 revenue growth by about $600M.
key_facts.excerpt: primarily driven by $5 billion of computing costs under short-term commitments and $2 billion of non-cash charges... reduced its revenue growth in the third quarter by about $600 million

key_facts.fact: The filing estimates 5% to 7% of nine-month revenue came from customers breaking usage rules or commercial terms, and warns its crackdown may reduce future revenue growth.
key_facts.excerpt: The filing estimated that 5% to 7% of the nine-month revenue came from customers breaking its usage rules or commercial terms

key_facts.fact: WSJ reports institutional investors told Anthropic its IPO valuation should be about $1.5T to $1.6T, below the ~$2T figures floated, after last week's tech selloff; the IPO is planned for later this month.
key_facts.excerpt: institutional investors told the Claude maker and its advisers that the company's valuation in its planned initial public offering later this month should be around $1.5 trillion to $1.6 trillion

key_facts.fact: Anthropic plans to list on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT and could start its roadshow as soon as next week.
key_facts.excerpt: plans to trade on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT... Anthropic could start marketing its shares as soon as next week and list from the week of 16 November.

stories.headline: MIT researchers: GPT-6 Astra edited 0.016% of a Qwen model's weights, raising math score 7.9% to 48.1%

key_facts.fact: Researchers including MIT's Omar Khattab published 'Sparks of Weight-Space Programming', arguing LLMs can natively read and write neural network weights without gradient-based training.
key_facts.excerpt: All of this is possible without allowing Astra to write training loops... We call this Weight-Space Programming.

key_facts.fact: Asked to make Qwen3.5-0.8B better at math, GPT-6 Astra traced its reasoning loops to one direction written by the MLPs of layers 15 and 19 and subtracted it from 131,072 weights, 0.016% of the model.
key_facts.excerpt: Astra traced the looping to one direction written by the MLPs of layers 15 and 19, and subtracted that direction from 64 output columns in each (131,072 weights)

key_facts.fact: With 50 forward passes, MATH-500 rose from 7.9% to 48.1%, GSM8K from 13.8% to 67.1% and IFEval instruction-following from 21.0% to 62.3%; answers hitting the token limit fell from 93% to 33.1%.
key_facts.excerpt: MATH-500 accuracy 7.9% -> 48.1%; GSM8K 13.8% -> 67.1%; IFEval 21.0% -> 62.3%; MATH-500 responses reaching the token limit 93.0% -> 33.1%

key_facts.fact: Astra worked through a CPU-only Python kernel over the weights, with no gradient descent, no internet and no access to the evaluation benchmarks.
key_facts.excerpt: We asked a frontier LLM ("Astra") to make Qwen3.5-0.8B better at math by editing its weights directly, with no gradient descent and no training.

key_facts.fact: An independent re-run of the published edited checkpoint on full MATH-500 scored 51.0%.
key_facts.excerpt: The edited model scored 51.0%, with 31.6% of answers hitting the token limit.

key_facts.fact: The authors say they are now building a benchmark and harness for LLMs to explore and write weights.
key_facts.excerpt: We think neural network weights will soon be natively optimized by LLMs that deliberately reason about the weights. We are now building a benchmark to evaluate, and a harness to help LLMs explore and write weights.

stories.headline: Salesforce agrees to buy voice-AI contact center startup Cresta, reportedly for $2.7B

key_facts.fact: Salesforce announced on Nov 2, 2026 a definitive agreement to acquire Cresta, which makes voice agents that resolve complex customer calls end to end and coach human representatives in real time.
key_facts.excerpt: Salesforce today announced it has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Cresta, the voice-first operating system for customer experience.

key_facts.fact: Salesforce did not disclose terms; The Information reported the price at $2.7 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Exclusive: Salesforce Acquires Startup Cresta for $2.7 Billion

key_facts.fact: Cresta's customers include Marriott, Comcast and Alaska Airlines; the deal is expected to close in the first quarter of Salesforce's fiscal 2028, subject to regulatory approvals.
key_facts.excerpt: operate at enterprise scale for leading brands including Marriott, Comcast and Alaska Airlines... expected to close in the first quarter of fiscal year 2028

key_facts.fact: Cresta will keep supporting rival contact center and telephony platforms after the deal closes.
key_facts.excerpt: After the transaction closes, Cresta will continue to support the leading contact center and telephony platforms its customers rely on today.

key_facts.fact: The deal follows Salesforce's 2026 purchases of Fin (about $3.6B) and Braze (about $5.66B), extending its push from digital support into phone calls.
key_facts.excerpt: Salesforce completed its roughly $3.6 billion Fin acquisition and agreed to buy Braze for about $5.66 billion

key_facts.fact: Kishan Chetan, EVP of Agentforce and Service Cloud, said voice is 'where service is hardest to get right, and where it matters most to customers.'
key_facts.excerpt: "Voice is where service is hardest to get right, and where it matters most to customers," said Kishan Chetan

stories.headline: China's planner says it will speed AI legislation and lifecycle safety standards for model makers

key_facts.fact: At a press conference on Nov 3, NDRC official Wang Ruomeng said China will accelerate foundational, comprehensive AI legislation and build a system of AI laws and regulations during the 15th Five-Year Plan.
key_facts.excerpt: 国家发展改革委创新和高技术发展司副司长王若蒙3日在新闻发布会上表示... 加快推进人工智能基础性综合性立法，构建人工智能法律法规体系

key_facts.fact: Wang said China will establish safety standards and ethical guidelines covering the full AI lifecycle, extending to data, computing power and algorithms, with periodic reviews to adjust rules as AI iterates quickly.
key_facts.excerpt: 要建立覆盖人工智能全生命周期的安全标准和伦理准则，同时要考虑到人工智能快速迭代特性，将对制度实施情况开展周期性评估

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg described the plan as some of the most comprehensive guidelines to guard against loss of control over increasingly powerful AI, encompassing developers from DeepSeek to Alibaba.
key_facts.excerpt: representing some of the most comprehensive guidelines to guard against a loss of control over increasingly powerful artificial intelligence... encompasses developers from DeepSeek to ... Alibaba Group

key_facts.fact: The effort would involve major developers including DeepSeek, Moonshot AI and Alibaba, which compete with OpenAI and Anthropic.
key_facts.excerpt: The regulatory effort would involve DeepSeek, 月之暗面 and Alibaba.

stories.headline: Trajectory raises $45M Series A led by Sequoia at $300M valuation for no-code model post-training

key_facts.fact: Trajectory raised a $45 million Series A at a $300 million valuation led by Sequoia, with Nvidia, Bessemer Venture Partners and Bain Capital Ventures participating.
key_facts.excerpt: raised $45 million in a Series A round at a $300 million valuation, led by Sequoia, with participation from Nvidia, Bessemer Venture Partners, and Bain Capital Ventures.

key_facts.fact: The 18-person startup, founded about a year ago by three Stanford classmates with DeepMind and Apple experience, lets non-technical specialists post-train open-source models from feedback (continual learning).
key_facts.excerpt: The 18-person company... founded about a year ago by three Stanford classmates with experience at Google DeepMind and Apple

key_facts.fact: Harvey and Rogo use Trajectory to post-train open-source models; other customers include Decagon, Mercor and Nvidia, and the platform is now publicly available.
key_facts.excerpt: Companies like Harvey and Rogo are already using Trajectory's platform... Trajectory's other customers include Decagon, Mercor, and Nvidia.

key_facts.fact: Co-founder Ronak Malde was among the Windsurf researchers acqui-hired by Google DeepMind; rivals include Thinking Machines Lab, Applied Compute (valued at $3.25B last month) and Prime Intellect.
key_facts.excerpt: He was among the handful of researchers Google DeepMind acqui-hired from Windsurf.

key_facts.fact: Trajectory opened a waitlist for its platform on launch day.
key_facts.excerpt: Sign up on our waitlist to get access to the Trajectory platform!

stories.headline: OpenAI to merge ChatGPT's Chat and Work tabs; ChatGPT and Codex to share one usage allowance

key_facts.fact: OpenAI told users by email it will merge the Chat and Work tabs in the ChatGPT desktop app, first for select users for feedback before a wide rollout.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI is now gearing up to merge the Chat and Work tabs within the ChatGPT experience, according to an email sent to users... available to select users for feedback before it is rolled out widely.

key_facts.fact: The email says users will be able to bring files and plugins and ask ChatGPT to build websites, create presentations or act on the web; Codex remains a separate experience.
key_facts.excerpt: You can bring in your files and plugins and ask ChatGPT to build a website, create a presentation, or do things for you on the web... Codex will remain a separate experience in the ChatGPT desktop app

key_facts.fact: ChatGPT and Codex will draw tokens from the same allowance pool, which OpenAI says may mean more frequent waits for resets for some users depending on usage and model.
key_facts.excerpt: both ChatGPT and Codex will draw tokens from the same allowance pool... some folks might need to wait for resets more frequently.

key_facts.fact: Rival Anthropic merged Claude's chat and Cowork functions into one screen in September.
key_facts.excerpt: Rival Anthropic merged Claude's chat and Cowork functions into one screen in September.
